C0.quote: A voting rule is a Condorcet extension if it returns a candidate
C0.note: Axiomatic study of voting rules (Condorcet extensions).

C1.quote: we provide an overview of Condorcet extensions and their inclusion relationships
C1.note: Impossibility and characterization results. The SAT-based proof and the simulation figure (Fig 4, computed with Ehrhart theory) are supporting.

C2.1.quote: a (preference) profile P = (≻i )i∈N over N is a collection of linear orders

C2.2.quote: a (preference) profile P = (≻i )i∈N over N is a collection of linear orders
C2.2.note: Margins derived from rankings are only a derived representation.

C2.3.quote: with ≻i denoting the preference of voter i ∈ N
C2.3.note: The paper speaks of voters' preferences. The profile is these preferences.

C2.4.quote: with ≻i denoting the preference of voter i ∈ N
C2.4.note: The rule is applied directly to preferences. Participation is defined via the voter's preference ≻j, with no statement on submission or reporting.

C3.1.quote: The participation axiom demands that voters are never better off by abstaining
C3.1.note: Participation concerns abstention, not misreporting a ranking. No analysis has voters submitting an input that differs from their held attitude.

C3.2.note: No statement that voters submit their held preferences.

C4.1.note: No utility, welfare or satisfaction notion is used for voters.

C4.2.note: The term 'dichotomous preferences' appears only in a reference title.

C5.1.note: The paper evaluates axioms such as reinforcement and participation and does not use the listed welfare criteria. Pareto-dominance appears only in a footnote remark. Choosing the Condorcet winner is a consistency property.

VOT.quote_behav: voter j should weakly prefer the outcome when j is present
VOT.note: Voters only join or leave the electorate in the axiom definitions. The model has no voter choosing actions strategically, so the axiom is treated as a property of the rule.

DES.note: The designer is not modelled explicitly.

C9.1.note: The claims are about which rule should be used.

C9.2.quote: maximin and its refinements are very attractive for threecandidate elections
C9.2.note: Recommending adoption in real elections needs an unstated assumption: that voters do not misreport rankings, since only no-show manipulation is addressed and the Gibbard-Satterthwaite theorem is cited only in the introduction. It also needs the assumption that the paradoxes studied are the relevant criteria for choosing a rule.
